contradictions.rationale: Within-source, roughly two minutes apart. At 16:56 he states that waiting for the session sometimes loses the trade entirely - 'the trade is completely gone from the direction, gone from the area where I was interested in taking'. At 18:51 he enumerates the outcomes of waiting and concludes 'there's no negative', listing only three cases: later entry but right direction, the loss you would have taken anyway, and a better entry. The forfeited-trade case he described himself is absent from the enumeration. The claim of no downside is therefore incomplete on the source's own evidence. Recorded, not resolved.

Within-source. The video's thesis, stated twice in the opening and again in the summary, is 'enter off of a confirmation, not an anticipation'. At 6:37 the instruction is that the 4-hour higher low 'is where you can then anticipate that wick fill'. This is the FOURTH record of the same inconsistency in Alex G's material (CLAIM|ALEX_G|20260728|033, |036, |047 and XCONTRA|20260728|003) and the first that is internal to a single source whose entire subject is the rule being broken. A possible reconciliation - that he anticipates the SETUP while still requiring a closed candle to ENTER - is coherent but is never stated by him, so applying it would be MOGO's reconciliation, not the educator's.

normalization.reversibilityProof: Reassembly of the recorded parts equals the source line; asserted for every transformed line at generation time.

openQuestions.reason: This source finally makes session timing an explicit, load-bearing rule - and the windows themselves are shown only as coloured bands on an on-screen session map, never spoken. Sydney, London and New York are named; no times are given. The gap recorded since source #2 ('trading at the right times') and source #4 ('the proper session') is now DOWNGRADED but NOT CLOSED: the rule exists and is prescriptive, but its parameters remain unstated. MOGO must not supply session hours - TJR's sessions are evidenced for TJR only.
openQuestions.text: Which exact hours are the high-volume windows Alex G will trade?

openQuestions.reason: No sample size, date range, instrument, timeframe or definition of 'bullish push'. Stated in passing as 'pretty much almost 70%'. Typed performance_hypothesis and structurally ineligible to become a rule candidate. It is, however, the most precisely specified setup in the source and therefore the most testable - see RC-25.
openQuestions.text: Is the ~70% next-day continuation figure measurable, and on what sample?

openQuestions.reason: The spoken content says $500 a day twice; the published YouTube title says $1000/day. Neither is evidenced, and no capital base, position size or sample is given. Recorded as a discrepancy between the source's own title and its content - MOGO does not choose between them.
openQuestions.text: Is the daily-income figure $500 or $1000, and on what capital?

openQuestions.reason: Fourth record of the same inconsistency, and the first internal to a source whose whole subject is the rule being broken. See the contradiction filed in this ingestion. Until resolved, neither the confirmation rule nor any anticipation exception may be promoted.
openQuestions.text: Does Alex G's method permit anticipating a setup, or require a closed candle first?

openQuestions.reason: He describes forfeited trades at 16:56 and then omits that case from the 'no negative' enumeration at 18:51. The claim is falsifiable and cheap to test: compare entry-on-confirmation against entry-at-next-session-open over the same signals. See RC-26.
openQuestions.text: What is the cost of waiting for the session, measured rather than asserted?

openQuestions.reason: Stated as 'an average of about 80 to 90 to even 100 pips'. No instrument, timeframe or method for choosing a target on a specific trade. It is nonetheless the FIRST target-shaped statement in five Alex G sources. Note also that it is expressed in PIPS - relevant to PROPOSAL-001, since MOGO is pip-native and TJR trades US indices.
openQuestions.text: Is 80-100 pips a target-selection rule, or a description of past averages?

openQuestions.reason: This source references a stop-loss repeatedly - 'where my stop loss would have been', 'more breathing room', 'better stop-loss' - and never states how it is placed. FIVE Alex G sources have now produced zero stop_rule and zero risk_rule claims, while this one names risk-to-reward as an input to a live decision. The gap is now demonstrably load-bearing rather than merely absent.

He says the candle 'has eaten the candlestick to the left' but also requires a 'body candlestick close above'. Body-engulfs-body and body-closes-beyond-range are different detectors that fire on different bars. Consistent with his body-based structure rule (CLAIM|ALEX_G|20260727|020), but not disambiguated here.
openQuestions.text: Must the engulfing candle's body engulf the prior body, or the prior candle's full range?

openQuestions.reason: 'The more dogeis that you would have, the more powerful' gives a direction but no count and no threshold at which behaviour changes. Same shape as the unquantified touch-count in source #3.
openQuestions.text: How many dojis constitute 'more powerful', and does the count change the decision?

openQuestions.reason: Pro-trend is stated as an absolute filter, but the trend's timeframe is not named here. Source #1 establishes a weekly/daily/4H hierarchy and source #4 requires two timeframes in sync; whether the pro-trend filter means the same thing is not stated.
openQuestions.text: On which timeframe is the trend that the confirmation must agree with?

openQuestions.reason: Level strength, timeframe, days remaining, risk-to-reward and other confluences are named as inputs to whether a second confirmation is required, with no thresholds. This step is explicitly discretionary and cannot be mechanised as stated.
openQuestions.text: At what values do the five named inputs change the decision?

openQuestions.reason: Presented as the way to tell a rejection from a forming higher low, but not stated as a mandatory step in the four-part summary at the end of the video.
openQuestions.text: Is the 4-hour cross-reference required on every setup, or only when a daily wick is ambiguous?

openQuestions.reason: Three overrides to an otherwise black-and-white day rule, none quantified. An unquantified override makes the rule it modifies unfalsifiable in practice.
openQuestions.text: What counts as a 'shorter' take-profit, a 'very strong' confirmation, or 'a lot of' momentum?
